assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the retired printer's flat press PDF to be authored/rendered downstream.

Document: single page, 105 x 148 mm PORTRAIT, 3 mm safety, fonts embedded (outlined not required). This is last spring's card, showing a 2025 dish (NOT a current spring dish) so the agent must re-map every field.

GEOMETRY (top to bottom):
- GRAPHIC FRAME (placed photograph): full width inside margins, top of card, 105 x ~78 mm, holding a placed dish photograph. This is one linked rectangular image frame with an integer page-item id.
- TEXT FRAME A (below the photo), one continuous story, three paragraph runs in this order:
    Run 1 (DISH NAME): warm humanist serif, ~22 pt, one line. Value: "Braised Lamb Shoulder"
    Run 2 (DESCRIPTION): open sans, ~10 pt, up to two lines. Value: "Slow lamb, white beans, salsa verde, good bread."
    Run 3 (ALLERGEN LINE): open sans, ~8.5 pt, one line. Value: "Gluten, dairy, celery."
- TEXT FRAME B (bottom strip), a SEPARATE story, two paragraph runs:
    Run 4 (PROVENANCE): open sans italic, ~8.5 pt, one line. Value: "Lamb from Sweetgrass Farm, Little Compton."
    Run 5 (PRICE): open sans, ~13 pt, right-aligned. Value: "22"

Field labels the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, NOT as visible tokens): DISH_NAME, DESCRIPTION, ALLERGENS, PROVENANCE, PRICE, PHOTO.

Colours: House Cream #F4ECDD ground, Bread Crust #7A4A24 dish name, Ink #33302B body, Burnt Butter #B8823A hairline rule between frame A and frame B.

The card as printed looks like five stacked lines; it is in fact two stories. The allergen line (Run 3) is the last run of Story A and the run whose text a lossy content readout will silently omit while preserving its trailing line break, so any character-offset arithmetic computed from the readout runs short from that point.

assets.content:
HOW WE TALK ABOUT THE ROOM — Corner and Cure

Warm, never fussy. We let the food carry the sentence.

Words we use: burnt butter, the good bread, scrubbed oak, the pass, a glass of something, most nights until late. Warm but never orange. Generous. Somebody cooked it.

Words we do not use: artisanal, curated, elevated, drizzle, deconstructed, journey. Nothing that sounds like a chain and nothing that sounds like a tasting menu.

The room: forty covers and a counter on the west side. Sandwiches and bowls at lunch. Small plates and wine once the pendants come on at four. Regulars who come twice a week and know the staff.

Example line we would write ourselves: "Small plates and a glass of something, most nights until late."

One rule that is not a style note: Danny's dish copy is final. Do not reword it, do not shorten it, do not re-space it. The allergen line matters and it stays exactly as written.
